items.title: docs(id): decision record for ESP32 hardware platform line (#5783)
items.body: Design-only record for #5783 (task 14116). Adds `doc/2026-11-09_design_id5783.md` — the first landed artifact for this issue. No production code. Covers, per the packet acceptance: - Board posture: one ESP32-S3 reference + compatibility envelope, measured against the bridge 64 KiB frame budget (§1, heap-margin invariant I-9). - Identity provisioning: device-owned identity via the #5884 ceremony, destroy-on-reset, stolen-device knowledge bounded by ceiling (§2). - Firmware lifecycle: flake-reproducible builds, offline-signed images, A/B OTA over HTTPS with rollback to last-good, checksummed device-side journal inherited from #2343 (§3). - Power: mains-first reference, battery as measured envelope, wake-storm avoidance as fleet property via per-device-seeded jittered backoff (§4). - Field behaviour: no-RTC untimed mode with bridge-assigned ingest time, bounded store-and-forward with gap signals, no portal click-through, two-slot checksummed writes (§5). - Open questions settled with named defaults: Q1 Rust/esp-idf + shared workspace crates; Q2 ESPHome interop-only; Q3 fake-device gates, bench informs; Q4 bench-first, reproducible-by-construction. - Invariants I-1–I-10; rejected alternatives with reasons; parent/sibling decisions (#2343, #5686, #5684/#5884, #5671) consumed, not re-decided (one correction: the setup-ceremony record is open PR #7850 for #5884, not merged — recorded accurately in the doc). Evidence baseline in the record header. Follows the `doc/YYYY-MM-DD_design_idNNNN.md` convention (cf. #5781, #5804). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: feat(id): id.device.v1 MQTT device bridge spec + labelled PoC (#2343)
items.body: Closes #2343. ## What The `id.device.v1` MQTT device-bridge **spec plus a labelled PoC**, exactly the remainder scoped by #2343's 2026-11-08 triage. Nothing here is production firmware or a production bridge. - **`doc/2026-11-09T05-00-00Z_feature_mqtt_device_bridge_id_device_v1/`** — the schema doc: topic table, per-world prefix, one connection per device, example documents for manifest / wants / cap-result / surface / events, wire bounds, and the recorded recommendations (retention, TLS + per-device credentials, reconnect/backoff, device-side journaling, minimum `time.tick`, closed firmware subset). - **`pkgs/id/src/device_bridge.rs`** — the PoC module (labelled as such in its module docs): topic helpers, fail-closed `Authenticator`, `Bridge::evaluate_wants` with the web refusal vocabulary, `FakeBroker` (retained manifest, retained-wants ban, wire bounds, auth), `FakeDevice` (journal across reconnects, 1 Hz tick floor, capped exponential backoff, encoder-as-`Key` with a signed delta). A real MQTT transport replaces `FakeBroker` without touching `Bridge` — that seam is the point of the PoC. ## Decisions reused from #5901 (not reopened) Retained manifest only · TLS plus per-device credentials · closed device subset (`device.info`, small `screen`/`text`, closed `form.*`, `loc.position` when GNSS present, key/encoder events) · bridge as translator. #2028 still defers production rollout; #5783 owns boards, firmware, OTA and power. Home Assistant interop is recorded as out-of-scope-but-supported. ## Bounds Reuses the host constants rather than restating them: 64 KiB `wants`/events, 8 KiB args. One finding worth noting: oversize args are rejected by `parse_wants` at parse time, before any per-request evaluation — the PoC test asserts that host boundary instead of inventing a per-request code that the host never emits. ## Tests ``` cargo test --lib device_bridge # 11 passed ``` Covering: topic shape, retained manifest for late subscribers, the full manifest→wants→result flow, unknown cap, ungranted cap, retained-wants rejection, oversize wants, oversize args at the host parse boundary, fail-closed auth (wrong token, unknown device, unauthenticated publish), minimum tick, backoff monotonicity/cap, encoder-to-`Key` delta. No production code paths are modified: `lib.rs` gains one `pub mod` line. items.title: fix(id/web): make SaveRateLimiter::acquire atomic vs completion (#9587)
items.body: Fixes #9587 (follow-up to PR #4193 / #2466). Queue task 16143. ## Problem `SaveRateLimiter::acquire` did its cooldown `check` (await, tokio mutex on `last_save`) and its in-flight reservation insert (a different std mutex) as two separate steps. A save completing between a second acquire's check and its insert — `complete()` calls `record()` and then Drop releases the reservation, in that order — admitted that acquire inside the just-recorded cooldown, re-opening the guarantee #4193 exists to enforce. Separately, `SavePermit::drop` released with `if let Ok`, so a poisoned in-flight lock would leave a filename reserved (and refused) forever, while `acquire` explicitly recovers poisoning via `into_inner()`. ## Fix - `acquire` re-validates the cooldown after taking the reservation. Because `complete()` records *before* Drop releases, any completion that raced the check/reserve gap has already recorded its cooldown by the time the reservation succeeds, so the re-validation observes it and refuses; a refused acquire releases the reservation it just took, leaving nothing behind. - `SavePermit::drop` recovers a poisoned lock with `into_inner()`, exactly like `acquire`. - The design doc (`doc/2026-11-02T07-00-00Z_design_save_reservations`) decision 1/3 wording now describes the re-validation mechanism instead of claiming the pair is taken under the in-flight lock. ## Tests - New deterministic interleaving regression (`test_save_limiter_acquire_refuses_when_a_save_completes_between_check_and_reserve`): locks and the tokio mutex's FIFO waiter order orchestrate a completion landing exactly between check and reserve — no sleeps or timing loops. Verified it **fails pre-fix** (temporary revert: panicked at the refusal assert) and passes post-fix. - New poisoned-Drop test (`test_save_limiter_permit_drop_recovers_a_poisoned_in_flight_lock`). - Limiter suite: **9/9 pass**. Full `id-web` lib suite: **651 passed, 1 failed** — `test_load_asset_urls_from_manifest` fails identically on clean `origin/main` in a bare worktree (web asset manifest not built there: `main_js` unhashed); pre-existing and unrelated. - `cargo fmt` clean. Clippy could not run in the pooled target dir (E0514 rustc-version mismatch between pooled artifacts and clippy-driver — environment, reproduced before any lint output on this crate). No 429 / "Try again in Ns" contract change; cooldown duration and client retry behaviour untouched, per the issue's scope exclusions. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Prevented overlapping saves from bypassing the cooldown. * Ensured filename reservations are released even when internal locking encounters an error.
